supporting_observations.claim: The alerted PowerShell process ran on WS-ICHEN-01 at 13:42:01 as NWD\sam.okafor, using the documented \FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1 command; its working directory was C:\Users\sam.okafor and its logon ID matches the preceding network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01.
The timing and command are consistent with the stated business-hours patching practice. The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update, and both processes then exited.

During the same patch activity, the workstation connected through the proxy to download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent and approximately 38.8 MB received, consistent with the update installation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The logs establish the PowerShell command line and associated process activity, but do not include the contents or hash of Apply-Updates.ps1.
The available records do not show the initiating process on WS-SOKAFOR-01 or independently verify the remote execution mechanism.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that Ivy Chen personally opened or interacted with the PowerShell window; the logged process ran as sam.okafor.
The evidence does not independently verify the contents of the downloaded update package or the script.
unrelated_findings: WS-ICHEN-01 accessed customer.cloud.com/Citrix/StoreWeb in Firefox; verify separately whether this Citrix access is authorized, since the inventory does not list it among approved services. This does not change the disposition of the patch-related PowerShell activity. (T044-00163, T044-00171, T044-00172)
Webex.exe was launched with an app.slack.com URL; consider checking separately whether this use is expected. (T044-00168, T044-00170)

DC-NWD-01 made connection attempts toward WS-ICHEN-01 on ports 8080, 443, 445, and 135; the recorded attempts were rejected or did not complete. Investigate separately if unexpected. (T044-00127, T044-00128, T044-00129, T044-00130, T044-00131, T044-00132, T044-00133, T044-00134)
